$comment: HAND-EDITED source of the Appearance section's theme, background, density, pane and focus ring rows (cx-d5b5d). scripts/cmux-next/gen-settings-sources.py writes the Swift descriptors and parser constants from it; its docstring is the row format (tabs.json's $comment repeats it, plus choices_from and "swift_case": null). Lists: SettingsSchema.all concatenates them, so rows keep the export's order; schemas/settings/settings-schema.json must not change when rows move here.

rows.note: cmux's terminal theme: a Ghostty theme name or a light/dark pair; unset is the Ghostty config's theme.

help.text: Colors for terminals. cmux uses them too while App Theme is Match Terminal Theme. A space, workspace or terminal theme overrides it.

summary.text: Colors for terminals, and cmux unless App Theme is set

rows.note: The theme of cmux's own surfaces; followTerminal (the default) uses the terminal theme.

help.text: Colors for the window, sidebar, tabs and cmux's pages. Terminals keep the Terminal Theme. Every color meets WCAG AA contrast.

summary.text: Colors for the window, sidebar, tabs and pages

help.text: Your color changes to a theme, such as "Rose Pine/background": "#1f1d2e". The theme itself never changes; remove an entry to reset that color.

rows.name: favorites

help.text: Themes starred in a theme picker. The picker lists them first.

rows.palette_hidden: a theme picker's stars edit it: a list of theme names

rows.name: rotation
rows.note: When launch turns appearance.theme to the next starred theme.

help.text: When cmux opens, the terminal theme changes to the next starred theme. Needs two starred themes, and has no effect while Match System Appearance is on.

summary.text: Change to the next starred theme

choices.note: The first launch of each day.

rows.note: Art Color (art) is no ThemeAccent: the accent takes the hue of the art a window shows (AccentSetting.artID).

help.text: The color of selection, focus and the Send button. Theme Color takes the theme's own hue, such as Rose Pine's iris.
A look from a file in ~/.config/cmux/themes, such as "tokyo" for tokyo.json. Its values apply over these settings, live as you save it. Unset, no file applies.
The color of selected text everywhere: terminals, Markdown, editors, the address bar and text fields. Unset, it is the terminal theme's selection color.

rows.note: Legacy: the bundled paintings (BackdropArt) follow None; appearance.background wins when both are set.

help.text: A public-domain painting behind the window material. Lower Opacity to reveal it. Attribution is linked above.

rows.page_hidden: legacy: the wallpaper card's appearance.background replaces it; the key still loads

rows.note: None and Shuffle Paintings, then the bundled art by collection and Desktop Wallpaper (BackdropSelectionSetting.catalogChoices).

help.text: Choose a public-domain painting, your desktop wallpaper, or a macOS system wallpaper behind the window material.
How often a shuffled background turns to its next picture.

summary.text: How often Shuffle changes the picture

help.text: Map stable display identifiers to daily, folder:<absolute path>, desktop, a fixed background, or none.
Map stable display identifiers to 15m, hourly, or daily. Unset displays use the global rotation.
One background behind the whole window, or a copy in each pane. A pane's own background (right-click a pane) shows either way.

summary.text: One background or one per pane

help.text: Draws windows in the plain theme color, without paintings, wallpapers or glass. Your background choices stay as they are and come back when you turn it off.
Applies Hue and Saturation to the window's tint. Off, they have no effect.
How much of the theme color covers the material behind the window.
Unset, the window follows Ghostty's background-opacity and background-blur.

summary.text: Clear Glass shows the desktop through the wallpaper

help.text: How much more theme color covers a window while another one is in front. 0 keeps the same look.
The glass takes the colors of your desktop picture and follows it when the picture or Space changes.

rows.name: glassTransparency

help.text: How much of the desktop or wallpaper shows through the glass.

rows.page_hidden: duplicates appearance.backgroundOpacity; the key still loads

help.text: Shift the tint color around the hue wheel.
Increase or reduce the tint color intensity.
Row height, padding, corners, icons and text size together. Compact is the default.

rows.palette_hidden: the Density card and the palette's density rows pick it
the Density card edits them: a list of density objects

help.text: Text size of tabs, the sidebar and other controls. Terminal text has its own size.
Text size of tabs, the sidebar and other controls. Terminal text has its own size.

summary.text: Text size of tabs, sidebar and controls

rows.page_hidden: opt-in: the Debug Settings toggle chrome.interfaceSize turns it on, until it is promoted

help.text: None removes every border, hairline and separator in the app.
How the focused pane stands out: its border, subtler tabs in the other panes, both or neither.

summary.text: How the focused pane stands out

help.text: How the other panes' tabs draw subtler when Focused Pane marks tabs: Fade dims them, Tonal steps their text down, Quiet keeps only a faint selected pill.

summary.text: How tabs in other panes tone down

rows.note: The window's look; its choices and their titles are schemas/settings/chrome-styles.json (ChromeStyleSetting+Choices.swift).

help.text: The look of the window: whether panes sit in one rounded card, and where lines are drawn. Separation, Sidebar Background and the sidebar border still win when you set them.
Splits, closes, moves, zooms, column scrolls and screen switches slide into place. Off: they change at once.
A new tab grows into its place in the tab bar. Off shows it there at once.
A new workspace row opens in the sidebar. Off shows it there at once.
None stops tabs, rows and panes exactly at their place. Subtle lets them settle with a small bounce.

rows.name: paneSeparation
rows.note: Unset follows the curved main pane (Metrics.defaultPaneSeparation).

help.text: How panes are told apart. None draws no border or divider at all; dragging between panes still resizes them. Default: dividers inside the curved main pane, borders otherwise.
One radius for panes, tabs, panels, popovers, cards and toasts. Shapes inside them use this radius minus the corner padding.
Space between a pane's edge and its tabs. Inner corners use the corner radius minus this.
